root_cause.text: The arm64 early kernel page-table allocator underestimated the number of page-table pages needed for 4K builds, because it did not account for the extra early-only split introduced by separately mapping [_text, _stext), allowing the early mapping to overflow into the gap page before early_init_stack.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `EARLY_SEGMENT_EXTRA_PAGES` from `(KERNEL_SEGMENT_COUNT + 1)` to `(KERNEL_SEGMENT_COUNT + 2)` and explicitly states that “since commit 5973a62efa34 … the early mapper also maps [_text, _stext) separately from [_stext, _etext). This adds one more early-only split and can require one more page-table page than the existing EARLY_SEGMENT_EXTRA_PAGES allowance reserves,” with the commit message showing the overflow into `init_pg_end`/the gap page before `early_init_stack`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reserve one additional early segment page to account for the extra kernel image split and unaligned boundary handling.
intent_record.what: The macro `EARLY_SEGMENT_EXTRA_PAGES` was changed from `KERNEL_SEGMENT_COUNT + 1` to `KERNEL_SEGMENT_COUNT + 2`, and a comment was added explaining that the early mapping has an extra split at `[_text, _stext)` and needs one additional page for unaligned `SWAPPER_BLOCK_SIZE` boundaries.
intent_record.how: This increases the number of reserved pages for early kernel segment mapping, preventing insufficient reservation when the initial mapping is split more than previously accounted for. It avoids potential layout/overflow issues during early boot VM mapping setup.

grouping_result.intent: Reserve one additional early segment page to account for the extra kernel image split and unaligned boundary handling.

relevance_review.reason: The change explicitly reserves an additional early page-table/page segment to account for an extra kernel image split and unaligned boundary handling, which matches the root cause of underestimating early page-table pages for 4K arm64 builds due to the separately mapped [_text, _stext) split.

candidates.rationale: This constant underpinned the early page-table page estimate; for 4K builds it failed to include the extra early-only split for separately mapping [_text, _stext), leading to too few pages being reserved.

This expression shows the pre-fix sizing logic for early segment page allocation; the vulnerability came from this logic not accounting for the additional split, so the allocator could overflow into the gap page before early_init_stack.

vuln_statements.explanation: This constant drove the early kernel page-table page count. With the extra early-only split for separately mapping [_text, _stext) on 4K builds, the value was too low and caused the allocator to reserve too few page-table pages.

This sizing expression used the underestimated segment count to compute the early page-table reserve. Because it did not account for the additional early split, the early mapping could overflow into the gap page before early_init_stack.
